title: The k = 3 Threshold and the Expected-Count Balance
content: The header frames the parent's OQ-03: for triple birthday coincidences among d days, the threshold group size is n ≈ (6 d² ln2)^(1/3). The heuristic is the expected-count balance — the expected number of triples C(n,3)/d² = n(n-1)(n-2)/(6d²) equals ln2 at the 50%-chance point, i.e. n(n-1)(n-2) = 6 d² ln2. The file proves the rigorous, machine-checked leading-order consequence of this single modeling assumption; it does not re-derive the balance from a Poisson limit theorem, so the boundary between proved mathematics and probabilistic heuristic is explicit.

title: Cube Roots as the Real Power t ↦ t^(1/3)
content: cubeRoot_cube establishes (x³)^(1/3) = x for x ≥ 0. Rather than develop a bespoke nth-root, the proof treats the cube root as the real power Real.rpow at exponent 1/3. The key move is rewriting 1/3 = (3:ℕ)⁻¹ so that Mathlib's Real.pow_rpow_inv_natCast applies — the general fact (xⁿ)^(n⁻¹) = x on the nonnegatives. This lemma is the bridge that lets the whole argument stay inside Mathlib's well-developed rpow API, where monotonicity and the inverse-of-power identity are already proved.

title: The Threshold Statement and Setup
content: birthday_triple_threshold states that any n ≥ 2 solving the balance equation satisfies (6d²ln2)^(1/3) ≤ n ≤ (6d²ln2)^(1/3) + 2. The setup abbreviates L = 6 d² ln2, records 0 < log 2 (Real.log_pos, since 1 < 2), and deduces 0 ≤ L by positivity, plus 0 ≤ n and 0 ≤ n−2 from n ≥ 2. These nonnegativity facts are exactly the side conditions that the cube-root lemma and rpow monotonicity demand, so collecting them up front keeps both branches of the sandwich short.

title: Lower Bound: L ≤ n³ Gives (6d²ln2)^(1/3) ≤ n
content: The lower branch uses the upper cube of the sandwich: n(n-1)(n-2) ≤ n³. Substituting the balance equation turns this into L ≤ n³; the inequality's slack is n³ − n(n-1)(n-2) = n(3n-2) ≥ 0, which nlinarith closes from the single product hint n·(3n−2) ≥ 0. Applying the monotone cube root (Real.rpow_le_rpow at exponent 1/3) and then cubeRoot_cube on the right gives L^(1/3) ≤ (n³)^(1/3) = n.
mathContext: $n(n-1)(n-2) \le n^3$ since $n^3 - n(n-1)(n-2) = n(3n-2) \ge 0$; cube-root $\Rightarrow L^{1/3} \le n$.

title: Upper Bound: (n−2)³ ≤ L Gives n ≤ (6d²ln2)^(1/3) + 2
content: The upper branch uses the lower cube: (n-2)³ ≤ n(n-1)(n-2) = L. The slack is n(n-1)(n-2) − (n-2)³ = (n-2)(3n-4) ≥ 0, again one product hint for nlinarith. Cube-rooting gives n − 2 = ((n-2)³)^(1/3) ≤ L^(1/3), and linarith adds 2 to reach n ≤ L^(1/3) + 2. The additive gap is exactly the difference between the cube roots of the two consecutive bounding cubes, hence the uniform constant 2.
mathContext: $(n-2)^3 \le n(n-1)(n-2)$ since the gap is $(n-2)(3n-4)\ge 0$; cube-root $\Rightarrow n-2 \le L^{1/3}$.

title: Packaged Threshold Gap
content: birthday_triple_threshold_gap restates the result as |n − (6d²ln2)^(1/3)| ≤ 2: the balance-equation solution is within a bounded, d-independent distance 2 of the leading-order threshold (6d²ln2)^(1/3). The proof simply unpacks the two-sided bound via abs_le and closes both halves with linarith. This is the rigorous form of the asymptotic n ≈ (6d²ln2)^(1/3) — the error term is O(1), uniformly in the number of days d.

title: Summary and axiom-free verification
content: The closing block records the file's three results — cubeRoot_cube ((x³)^(1/3) = x for x ≥ 0), birthday_triple_threshold (the two-sided sandwich (6d²ln2)^(1/3) ≤ n ≤ (6d²ln2)^(1/3) + 2), and birthday_triple_threshold_gap (the packaged |n − (6d²ln2)^(1/3)| ≤ 2) — and answers the parent's OQ-03: the k = 3 (triple-coincidence) threshold is (6d²ln2)^(1/3) to leading order with a bounded, d-independent additive error at most 2, proved by the cube-root sandwich (n−2)³ ≤ n(n−1)(n−2) ≤ n³. The trailing #print axioms commands are the machine-checked confirmation of the 0-axiom claim: both main theorems reduce to the foundational axioms alone, with no sorry and no native_decide.
mathContext: $n \approx (6 d^2 \ln 2)^{1/3}$, rigorously $\bigl|n-(6d^2\ln 2)^{1/3}\bigr|\le 2$; verified axiom-free via $(n-2)^3 \le n(n-1)(n-2) \le n^3$.
